stories.title: Punjab govt bans use, sale of camera-enabled smart glasses for 30 days
summary: LAHORE: The Punjab government issued an order on Tuesday banning the use and sale of camera-enabled smart glasses and miniature cameras “disguised as everyday objects” for 30 days.
The ban comes a day after the Punjab government announced its plan to impose the restriction.
Taking up the plea on Thursday, the LHC directed the federal government to forward a summary to the federal cabinet regarding the unregulated import and sale of smart glasses.

stories.title: Maldives president arrives in Pakistan for three-day visit
summary: Maldives President Dr Mohamed Muizzu arrived in Islamabad on Tuesday on a three-day visit to Pakistan, according to a statement from his office.

Meanwhile, the Maldivian delegation, led by Foreign Minister Iruthisham Adam and comprising cabinet ministers and senior officials, arrived in Islamabad earlier on Tuesday ahead of President Muizzu’s arrival, the Foreign Office (FO) said in a statement.
In 2015, former Maldivian president Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom undertook a two-day state visit to Pakistan on May 6-7 at the invitation of then-premier Nawaz Sharif.

stories.title: Main suspect accused of visa fraud in student's suicide case killed in firing by accomplices: police
summary: ISLAMABAD: The prime suspect accused of defrauding a 20-year-old student, who allegedly died by suicide, was killed after being shot by his accomplices in Islamabad on Tuesday, claimed police.
According to the Islamabad police spokesperson, the prime suspect sustained injuries when his accomplices opened fire on cops in the jurisdiction of Ramna police station.

It was then that four of the main suspect’s accomplices, who were on two motorcycles, “opened indiscriminate fire on the police party in an attempt get the main suspect freed”, the spokesperson added.

stories.title: Pakistani national who allegedly defrauded US Postal Service of $126m arrested in Lahore: NCCIA
summary: LAHORE: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency said on Tuesday that a prime suspect in a case involving the sale of counterfeit US postage stamps had been arrested in Lahore.

He said the suspect operated a website — LabelsBank.com — from August 2023 to September 2026 and used it to market and sell counterfeit US postage stamps online. “More than five million stamps were sold through the website at a price of around $2 per stamp.
Money trail Flanked by Lahore NCCIA Deputy Director Waqas Saeed, Ameer said that 16 bank accounts had been used in the scam.

stories.title: Govt ups petrol price by Re0.88 per litre, high-speed diesel rate by Re0.53
summary: Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

stories.title: Judicial commission points finger at police’s ‘epic failure’, says Mir Raza was murdered
summary: KARACHI: A judicial commission formed to investigate the circumstances and possible negligence in businessman Mir Raza Ali’s murder case has pointed out the police’s “epic failure” in their investigation.
The meeting was attended by Medico-Legal Officer (MLO) Dr Osama Sheikh, who conducted Ali’s first autopsy, the Karachi police chief and other senior officials.

The inquiry report, along with associated documents, was handed over to the focal person of the provincial government and Home Department Additional Secretary Javed Ahmed Abro by the commission registrar, Abdul Majid, on the premises of the SHC.

stories.title: All-round Arafat Minhas owns the show as Pakistan crush England in tri-series match
summary: Pakistan pacer Haris Rauf celebrates dismissing England opener Tom Banton.—AFP Arafat continued his dismantling of the lower order, dismissing Jamie Overton for one when Hasan Nawaz took a catch at long-on after the batter charged down the pitch.

England captain Harry Brook looks stunned after being cleaned up by Pakistan’s Arafat Minhas.—AFP “Banton and Ducky set the tone beautifully, but we lost the wickets in clumps and could not put on a partnership and ended up on the wrong side,” Brook said.

Pakistan’s Arafat Minhas (L) and Faheem Ashraf run between the wickets.—AFP Faheem Ashraf then provided a late surge with 39 off 26 balls, and captain Shaheen’s brisk five-ball 10 helped Pakistan cross 300.

stories.title: Multan court grants police 3-day physical remand of suspect accused of hitting, killing teenage worker with his car
summary: LAHORE: A Multan court on Tuesday granted police three-day physical remand of a suspect accused of killing a 15-year-old boy in the city.

Later, Multan City Police Officer (CPO) Akhtar Farooq said while speaking to the media that raids were being conducted for the arrest of a second suspect. “We all are in deep pain,” the CPO said, adding that the orphan boy had been “subjected to barbarity”.

His cousin told police that the boy had reportedly faced violence and threats by the suspects, the FIR said, adding that the 15-year-old was fleeing when the suspects pursued him in a car and hit him.

stories.title: On-duty cop martyred in firing by attackers in KP's Miranshah: police
summary: District Police Officer (DPO) Sajjad Hussain confirmed the details to Dawn, saying that additional SHO Meera Khan was targeted when he was on duty. “He sustained multiple bullet wounds and succumbed to his injuries,” the DPO said.

It was a day after four Federal Board of Revenue officials were martyred in firing by unidentified men, while a separate attack on a highway traffic police vehicle left a police official martyred and another injured in Dera Ismail Khan.

On Sept 27, 14 people, including two rescue officials, were martyred and 35 sustained injuries after a suicide bomber rammed an explosive-laden vehicle into a police checkpost in and then targeted an ambulance taking bodies to hospital in DI Khan.

stories.title: PHC seeks replies from KP govt, IG on Sohail Afridi, other PTI leaders' detention
summary: PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Tuesday sought replies from the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government and senior police personnel, including the inspector general (IG), regarding non-functional provincial chief executive Sohail Afridi’s detention.

The petitioner sought directives for the respondents concerned to submit a comprehensive report regarding the whereabouts, present condition and legal status of Afridi, as well as the details of steps taken to trace and recover him.

They contended that the whereabouts and present condition of PTI leaders needed to be immediately ascertained through lawful means, and requested the PHC to issue directives for their release if they were found to be in unlawful custody.

stories.title: At SCO, Dar calls for promoting use of national currencies to help offset global economic shocks
summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday encouraged members of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) to use national currencies for “mutual settlement” and establish other financial mechanisms to “offset international financial shocks”.

In the joint communiqué for the Pakistan-chaired 2024 CHG meeting, SCO member states had reaffirmed the need for consistent implementation of a roadmap on gradual increase in the share of national currencies in mutual settlements.
On Sept 30, Dar reviewed preparations for the CHS summit as SCO national coordinators, who were in Islamabad for a meeting, called on him.

stories.title: Indian military doctrines with 'poor' strategic sense of nuclear realities endanger South Asia: NCA adviser
summary: The outcome is very risky and delusional Indian military doctrines with a poor strategic sense of nuclear realities are endangering South Asia and beyond,” he said in his key note address at a workshop titled ‘Nuclear Deterrence and Strategic Stability in South Asia’.

The security perceptions in South Asia had not evolved in a vacuum, Jamil continued. “Indian revisionist and hegemonic political aspirations have [a] long history of Indian coercion and militant violence against all [of] its neighbours.
The Indian strategic approach, he said, sought political and military dominance to be a “regional hegemon with a revisionist political thinking”.

stories.title: Brent falls as Iran's president discusses mediation with CDF Munir
summary: The November contract for US West Texas Intermediate crude, which expired on Tuesday, settled ​down $1.87, or 1.8%, at $101.79.
Iran's President Pezeshkian discussed mediation efforts ⁠and regional developments during a meeting with Field Marshal Munir in Tehran, Iran's Nournews reported on Tuesday.
US crude oil stockpiles ⁠were expected ​to have fallen last week along with product inventories, an extended Reuters poll showed ​on Tuesday.

stories.title: North Korean state media releases photos of Kim Jong Un amid death rumors
summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un appeared in photos released by state media on Tuesday after rumours circulated on social media claiming he had died of a brain haemorrhage.
North Korean state media regularly publishes photos of Kim and reports on his activities.
Rumours about Kim's death have circulated before, as North Korea's limited access to information makes it difficult to independently verify reports about the country's leadership.

stories.title: US VP Vance says he is staying out of Israel vote as Trump backs Netanyahu
summary: US Vice President JD Vance said he would not be following Donald Trump in endorsing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and wanted to stay on the sidelines. “I’m not anti-endorsing him.

I’m not getting involved in Israeli elections,” Vance said of Netanyahu, in an interview on Monday with journalist Mark Halperin. “I endorse American candidates and that’s where I’m focused on is the (US) midterms,” he added.
Trump on Sunday issued a public endorsement of his right-wing ally Netanyahu, who is seeking a new term as premier in Israel’s Oct 27 parliamentary election.

stories.title: New AI tool can predict cancer survival chances from selfie: study
summary: US researchers have developed an artificial intelligence (AI) tool that can predict cancer patients' survival chances from a single facial photograph, according to a study published on Monday in the journal The Lancet Digital Health.

Developed by researchers at Mass General Brigham in the US state of Massachusetts, the system, called FAHR-Face, analyses facial features to estimate biological age and mortality risk, potentially helping doctors make treatment decisions.

The model was trained on more than 40 million facial photos and adapted into two tools: FAHR-FaceAge, which estimates biological age, and FAHR-FaceSurvival, which predicts cancer patients' survival directly from facial images without relying on age estimates.

stories.title: US judge dismisses Sam Altman's sister's sexual abuse lawsuit
summary: Sam Altman on Tuesday won the dismissal ​of a civil lawsuit filed by his sister accusing the ‌OpenAI co-founder and chief executive of repeated sexual abuse more than two decades ago, an accusation he denies.
She ​said the last acts of sexual abuse and rape ​occurred when ⁠Sam Altman was an adult.
Sam ⁠Altman has ​said she began accusing him on social ​media of sexual abuse after the family rejected her demands for more funds.

stories.title: Govt increases petrol by 88 paisas, diesel by 53 paisas per litre for Oct 21
summary: The federal government on Tuesday increased the price of petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) by 88 paisas and 53 paisas per litre, respectively, for October 21.

On September 13, PM Shehbaz announced a special relief scheme offering Rs100 per litre off petrol for motorcycles, three-wheeler rickshaws and cars with engines up to 800cc, in an attempt to shield lower-income consumers from the impact of rising petroleum prices.

Oil prices ​slipped after touching a five-month high on Tuesday as traders weighed a meeting between the Iranian president and ‌Pakistan's army chief, a key US-Iran mediator, against continued Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf.

stories.title: Primary suspect in Laiba Ejaz suicide case dies after being shot by accomplices: police
summary: The primary suspect in the case involving the suicide of former International Islamic University Islamabad (IIUI) student Laiba Ejaz died after being wounded by gunfire from his own accomplices during an exchange of fire with police in Islamabad.

Read: Islamabad student found dead after allegedly losing Rs7m in education scam Nauman was wounded by gunfire from his own accomplices, the spokesperson said, adding that police personnel remained unharmed due to their bulletproof jackets and other precautionary measures.

Laiba, who had aspired to study at a top US university, was found hanging from a tree near a road in Islamabad on October 9, after her family allegedly lost around Rs7 million to a consultant who had promised to secure her admission and a scholarship.

stories.title: Pakistan committed to fiscal reforms and sustainability, President Zardari tells IMF delegation
summary: President Asif Ali Zardari on Tuesday reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to fiscal sustainability, energy sector reforms, privatisation and social protection, saying the government was pursuing inclusive and green economic growth.

Azour acknowledged Pakistan’s continued engagement with the IMF under the ongoing programme and stressed the need to sustain reforms to strengthen macroeconomic stability, maintain fiscal discipline and support sustainable economic growth.
Earlier this month, Pakistan and the Fund reached a staff-level agreement following the fourth review under the EFF and the third review under the RSF.

stories.title: Defamation tribunal orders Punjab Assembly opposition leader to pay Rs3m to Azma Bokhari
summary: LAHORE: The Punjab Defamation Tribunal on Tuesday ruled in favour of Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari in a defamation suit against Punjab Assembly Opposition Leader Moeen Riaz Qureshi, ordering him to pay Rs3 million in general damages.
In January, Bokhari filed the defamation suit against Qureshi seeking damages of Rs800 million.
The information minister had filed the suit following allegations Qureshi levelled at the time of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s then-chief minister Sohail Afridi’s visit to the Punjab Assembly.

stories.title: ECONOMY: The Missing Entrepreneur of Sindh
summary: Sindh’s sugar mills, cotton ginning and rice milling show that agricultural wealth did become industrial capital.

Much of Sindh’s Hindu mercantile and entrepreneurial class migrated to India, while Muslim migrants from different parts of the Subcontinent brought new commercial skills, networks and capital to Karachi.
Sindh generated considerable wealth at both ends of its economy: agricultural wealth in the countryside and commercial and industrial wealth in Karachi.

stories.title: Toll on trade
summary: A YEAR after Islamabad severed commercial ties with Kabul over security concerns, the border trade disruption is taking a growing toll on KP, where livelihoods, businesses, farm markets, and a large number of workers depend on cross-border commerce.
Islamabad has valid security concerns — the Taliban must prevent Afghan territory from being used for attacks on Pakistan.
It should also assess the losses of traders, transporters, and farmers, and help businesses find new markets.

stories.title: Meet the heat storm: 7 takeaways from Reuters investigation that gave supersized heat waves a new name
summary: 2020s: The 10 largest heat storms mark a new era, with massive, cascading heat events touching virtually every person on the planet.
Photo: REUTERS Greenhouse gas emissions As greenhouse gas emissions have increased, so too have heat storms and ordinary heat waves.
Over that time, the average portion of the planet likely to be covered by heat storms and heat waves has risen more than 12-fold.

stories.title: NCCIA arrests Khanewal man indicted in $126m US postal fraud case
summary: According to the NCCIA, Akram allegedly operated the scheme from August 2023 till last month, selling counterfeit shipping labels for around $2 each.

It allegedly offered counterfeit postage at a fixed price, irrespective of a parcel’s weight, size or destination, allowing customers to ship packages at rates substantially below legitimate postal charges.
US court records showed that more than 5,200 people had used the website to purchase over 5.1 million counterfeit shipping labels.

stories.title: UK to deploy fighter jets to help protect Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
summary: British fighter planes will be deployed to help Saudi Arabia defend itself against increasing attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels, the UK government announced on Tuesday.
Yemen’s civil war — in which Saudi Arabia has led a military coalition supporting the government since 2015 — reignited in September after the collapse of a years-long truce.
Saudi Arabia, the Yemeni government and the United States accuse Iran of backing the Houthis — an allegation Tehran denies.

stories.title: Rubio says India made 'substantial progress' in diversifying oil purchases
summary: He has visited Uzbekistan, where he called for stronger partnerships with Central Asian countries, before landing in Mumbai for talks with Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar and meetings with business leaders.

India is a major importer of Russian oil, and US President Donald Trump’s tariff war launched in April last year has added to friction between Washington and New Delhi. “Obviously, we think we could be a source of some of their energy inputs,” Rubio said.

The top US diplomat will visit Jamnagar, in the western state of Gujarat, a port and stronghold of billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance conglomerate and its flagship refinery, the world’s largest. “India is a refining superpower,” said Rubio.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz ready to build consensus on counterterrorism if opposition willing to: Sanaullah
summary: Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah on Tuesday said the federal government was ready to invite all political parties and build consensus on counterterrorism.

The PM’s aide’s remarks come after the Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on October 11, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism.
The minister said controlling terrorism in KP was practically impossible without the provincial government’s full cooperation with federal institutions, the Pakistan Army and security agencies.

stories.title: France to deploy troops, admits to failures over weekend unrest
summary: France will reinforce police with troops and mount a huge security operation for ​more protests planned on Saturday, the government said on Tuesday, acknowledging failures in its response to last weekend's violence.

Targeted curfews help restore calm Framing the crisis as a choice "between violence and the Republic", Lecornu blamed the unrest on far-left groups, who ​in turn have accused the government of underestimating public anger over high living costs and declining public services.

Though not on the scale seen in France, the unrest nonetheless jolted Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government, which was ​expected to introduce new security ⁠measures at a cabinet meeting on Tuesday.

stories.title: Trump's approval falls to record low of 31% as midterms near, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
summary: President Donald ‌Trump's approval rating fell to a record low as Americans worried about high gasoline prices and appeared ready to punish his Republican Party in the November 3 congressional elections, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll that closed on Monday.
A Reuters/Ipsos poll two weeks earlier showed Democrats leading Republicans by 7 points, 44% to 37%.
Reuters/Ipsos poll of registered US voters nationwide Much of the drop in support for Republican congressional candidates was due to a larger ​share of women saying they ​would pick Democrats.

stories.title: Maldives president lands in Pakistan for three-day state visit
summary: Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu arrived in Islamabad on Tuesday for a three-day state visit to Pakistan from October 20 to October 22, at the invitation of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, according to state media.

The statement added that the state visit was the first by a president of the Maldives to Pakistan in 11 years and assumed special significance as the two countries commemorate the 60th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations in 1966.

The FO further added that Pakistan and Maldives enjoyed warm and fraternal relations rooted in shared faith, mutual respect, longstanding goodwill and close cooperation at regional and international forums.

stories.title: Mir Raza’s final hours: A trail of calls, a Rs30m plea and a vanishing act
summary: Two minutes later, at 4:09am, Salwa informed Mir Raza’s friend Haitham that all his social media accounts had been deleted.
At 4:38:27am on July 28, Mir Raza was last seen on CCTV footage from a rent-a-car office on Hill View Road.

The timeline leaves several questions unanswered: what prompted Mir Raza’s request for Rs30 million, why his social media accounts disappeared within hours, and what happened after he was last captured on CCTV.

stories.title: Turkiye submits Makkah defence pact to parliament for ratification, sources say
summary: Turkiye has submitted a defence ‌pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia to parliament for ratification, three parliamentary sources said on Tuesday, moving NATO's second-largest army closer to a formal mutual defence pledge with Riyadh as it faces Houthi attacks.
The three countries signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in August, under which an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all.

Turkiye, which has a robust defence industry, has condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, expressed willingness to help meet Riyadh's military technology needs and agreed to join ‌a Saudi-led ⁠coalition to ensure navigational safety in the Red Sea.

stories.title: Punjab govt reschedules Basant 2027 in Lahore for second time, sets March dates
summary: The Punjab government has rescheduled Basant 2027 in Lahore for a second time, with the provincial cabinet approving March 12, 13 and 14 as the new dates for the festival.
Read: Govt plans int'l standard Basant Maryam had announced the January dates as an extended celebration intended to promote Punjab’s cultural heritage and Lahore’s traditional identity.
The Lahore district administration has said kite flying will be permitted only on designated festival dates.

stories.title: Death toll from Houthi attack on Yemen training camp rises to 73
summary: An attack by Yemen's Houthi movement on a government security forces training camp in Shabwa province killed 73 people, the provincial media ​office said, raising the toll from Monday's strike as fighting ‌intensifies.
Read: Houthi attack kills 53 at Yemen government training camp, officials say Local authorities said three ⁠ballistic missiles hit security forces on Monday during training.
Yemeni government forces began a ​campaign this month to retake Houthi-held areas, recovering ground near the strait.

stories.title: Jon Stewart signs on to continue as ‘The Daily Show’ host through 2028
summary: Comedian Jon Stewart will continue hosting Comedy Central's "The Daily Show" on Mondays and serving as an executive producer through 2028, Skydance Television said on Monday.
"We are excited to continue our partnership with Jon and his award-winning news team," George Cheeks, co-chair and chief content officer of Skydance Television, said in a statement.
The Daily Show did not have a permanent host in 2023, instead using a rotating lineup of guest hosts that included Leslie Jones, Michael Kosta and Chelsea Handler.

stories.title: Balochistan govt rejects comparison with K-P, says cooperating with Centre on combatting terrorism
summary: The Balochistan government on Tuesday rejected comparisons with the former provincial government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (K-P), stating that, unlike the latter, it was cooperating with the federal government in the fight against terrorism.

He said the Balochistan government stood firmly with security forces and stressed that success in the fight against terrorism required cooperation among provincial administrations, the federal government and security institutions.
The officials reiterated that the provincial government would continue working with security forces to combat terrorism and improve security across Balochistan.

stories.title: Health ministry gets Momin Agha as 9th secretary in 19 months
summary: ISLAMABAD: The health ministry has again gotten a new secretary, with the Establishment Division notifying Momin Agha as the new administrative head.

According to a notification issued by the Establishment Division on Monday, available with Dawn, Agha “has been transferred and posted as secretary health with immediate effect and until further orders”.
Agha was removed as petroleum secretary in January 2026 and directed to report to the Establishment Division without a further posting.

stories.title: Deepika Padukone, Ranveer Singh reveal second daughter's name
summary: Bollywood actors Deepika Padukone and Ranveer Singh have revealed the name of their second daughter, Devi Padukone Singh, sharing a heartwarming family photograph on Instagram to mark Dussehra.

The photograph offered fans a rare glimpse into the couple's family life, showing Deepika cradling their newborn while Ranveer held their elder daughter, Dua, who affectionately kissed her younger sister.
In November that year, Deepika and Ranveer revealed her name and shared her first photograph, explaining that Dua represented the feeling of their prayers being answered.

stories.title: PHC issues notices in petitions challenging governor’s rule, emergency in KP; hearing adjourned till Nov 10
summary: PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court (PHC) on Tuesday issued notices to the federal and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa governments in several petitions challenging the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province on Oct 11.

Barrister Sameer argued that a resolution passed by the provincial assembly was mandatory for imposing governor’s rule and emergency. “No approval was obtained from the provincial assembly,” he told the court.
Following the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in the province, the federal government formed an 11-member technocratic KP Advisory Council.
